ai.description: This frog reaches 40–50 mm. It features a bright golden-yellow dorsum, a dark lateral stripe, and long, slender limbs. Distinctive white lip lines and pointed snouts aid identification.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hylarana urbis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous white upper lip stripe that extends clearly to the shoulder, unlike similar sympatric species.
ai.habitat: *Hylarana urbis* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near streams and riparian vegetation at elevations above 600 meters.
ai.behavior: The Urban Golden-backed Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates among damp leaf litter and urban vegetation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hylarana urbis* breeds during the monsoon season, laying large clutches of small, pigmented eggs in stagnant or slow-moving water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hylarana urbis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically occurring in the states of Karnataka and Kerala at elevations between 700 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Urban Golden-backed Frog produces a series of rapid, high-pitched "tink-tink" chirps, typically heard near stagnant water or urban drainage ditches.
